claim_reviews.conclusion: The split remains materially useful: steker is an Indonesian dictionary term, while palam is a Malaysian Malay dictionary term for the electrical connector. Malaysian Malay also has plag, but this does not make steker and palam the same national answer.
claim_reviews.subject: national split and overlap

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Electrical plug” and “plug inserted into an electrical socket” accurately identify the object and distinguish it from a socket or outlet.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: Steker is an established Indonesian term for the connector fitted to the end of an electrical cable and inserted into an electrical opening.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: steker

claim_reviews.conclusion: Palam is an established Malaysian Malay term for a two- or three-pin electrical device inserted into a socket; the definition matches the learner sense.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian Malay answer: palam

claim_reviews.conclusion: different-common-word is appropriate because the proposed answers are distinct standard/localized terms across the two varieties, despite additional shared or borrowed informal vocabulary.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: The reviewed dictionary sources establish the terms and meanings but do not provide comparable frequency data for informal shared use of English plug in both varieties.
claim_reviews.subject: final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No false-friend contrast is needed. The main possible ambiguity is polysemy: Malay palam can also mean a stopper or plug for a hole, but the electrical cue and definition disambiguate it; this is not a cross-variety false-friend error.
claim_reviews.subject: false-friend contrast

response.rationale: The national split is not materially overstated. Indonesian steker and Malaysian Malay palam are distinct established terms for the electrical plug; shared English-derived forms may occur informally, but available evidence does not support treating them as equally ordinary national answers. The cue, sense, answers, and relation are aligned. No false-friend contrast is required.
